nodes.title: Bible Structure
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that the Bible is one book made of many books divided into the Old and New Testaments and state that it contains 66 books.

nodes.title: Books of the Bible
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name books of the Bible in order and identify whether a given book belongs to the Old or New Testament.

nodes.title: Old & New Testament Divisions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can sort Bible books into their major divisions (Law, History, Wisdom/Poetry, Prophets; Gospels, Acts, Epistles, Revelation) and describe what each division contains.

nodes.title: Finding a Verse (Book, Chapter, Verse)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can read a Scripture reference and locate the correct book, chapter, and verse in a Bible.

nodes.title: Bible Translations
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that the Bible was written in original languages and translated into English, and identify common translations (e.g., KJV, NIV, ESV).

nodes.title: Memory Verses
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can recite a memorized Bible verse together with its reference and explain in simple terms what it means.

nodes.title: Reading Scripture Independently
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can look up a passage on their own, read it aloud, and summarize what it says in their own words.

nodes.title: Understanding Context
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify who wrote a passage, to whom, and why, and explain how the surrounding verses affect its meaning.

nodes.title: Biblical Interpretation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply basic interpretation principles (genre, context, comparing Scripture with Scripture) to explain the intended meaning of a passage.

nodes.title: Biblical Languages (Intro)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that the Old Testament was written mainly in Hebrew and the New Testament in Greek, and describe how word studies aid interpretation.

nodes.title: Creation & the Fall
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell the account of Creation and the Fall in Genesis and explain that sin entered the world through Adam and Eve's disobedience.

nodes.title: Noah & the Flood
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell the story of Noah and the Flood and explain the meaning of God's covenant sign of the rainbow.

nodes.title: Abraham & the Patriarchs
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe God's covenant with Abraham and identify Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph as the patriarchs who followed him.

nodes.title: Moses & the Exodus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell how God used Moses to lead Israel out of slavery in Egypt, including the plagues, the Passover, and the crossing of the Red Sea.

nodes.title: The Ten Commandments
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can list the Ten Commandments and explain that God gave them to Israel at Mount Sinai as a guide for living.

nodes.title: Israel's Kings: Saul, David & Solomon
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify Saul, David, and Solomon as Israel's first kings and describe a key event from each reign.

nodes.title: The Prophets
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what a prophet did, name several major and minor prophets, and describe the kind of message prophets brought to Israel.

nodes.title: The Exile & Return
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain why Israel and Judah went into exile, name Babylon as the empire that conquered Judah, and describe the return to rebuild Jerusalem.

nodes.title: The Psalms & Proverbs
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that Psalms are songs and prayers and Proverbs are short sayings of wisdom, and identify an example of each.

nodes.title: Old Testament Survey
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can place the major Old Testament events in order from Creation to the return from exile and explain how they form one unfolding story.

nodes.title: The Life of Jesus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can outline the main events of Jesus' life: His birth, baptism, ministry, death, and resurrection.

nodes.title: The Parables of Jesus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell a parable of Jesus (e.g., the Good Samaritan or the Prodigal Son) and explain the lesson it teaches.

nodes.title: The Miracles of Jesus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe several miracles of Jesus and explain what they showed about His identity and compassion.

nodes.title: The Death & Resurrection of Jesus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell the events of Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection and explain that Christians celebrate the resurrection at Easter.

nodes.title: The Four Gospels
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name the four Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John) and explain that each tells the account of Jesus' life and ministry.

nodes.title: The Early Church (Acts)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe how the Church began at Pentecost with the coming of the Holy Spirit and how the first Christians lived and spread the gospel.

nodes.title: Paul's Missionary Journeys & Letters
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain who Paul was, describe his missionary journeys, and identify several letters (epistles) he wrote to the churches.

nodes.title: The Book of Revelation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that Revelation is apocalyptic writing about the return of Christ and God's final victory, and describe its central hope of a new heaven and new earth.

nodes.title: New Testament Survey
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can place the major New Testament events in order from the Gospels through Acts, the Epistles, and Revelation and explain how they connect.

nodes.title: Key Bible Stories
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell several well-known Bible stories and identify the main person and lesson in each.

nodes.title: Elijah the Prophet
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe who Elijah was and retell a key event from his life, such as the contest with the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.

nodes.title: Daniel in Exile
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe who Daniel was and retell a key event, such as Daniel in the lions' den or his stand for faithfulness in Babylon.

nodes.title: Mary, Mother of Jesus
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe who Mary was and explain her role in the birth of Jesus.

nodes.title: Peter the Apostle
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe who Peter was as one of Jesus' disciples and retell a key event from his life in the Gospels or in Acts.

nodes.title: Key Bible Events Timeline
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can arrange the major events of the Bible in chronological order from Creation to the early Church.

nodes.title: Basic Biblical Themes
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify major biblical themes such as God's love, creation, sin, redemption, and covenant, and give an example of each from a story.

nodes.title: Doctrinal Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain core Christian beliefs about God, Jesus, the Bible, salvation, and the Church in their own words.

nodes.title: The Gospel & Salvation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the gospel: that Jesus died and rose to save people from sin, and that salvation is received by grace through faith in Him.

nodes.title: The Trinity
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that Christians believe in one God in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

nodes.title: Attributes of God
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name and explain attributes of God such as holy, loving, all-powerful, all-knowing, and eternal.

nodes.title: Sin & Grace
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what sin is, that all people have sinned, and how God's grace offers forgiveness through Jesus.

nodes.title: The Holy Spirit
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain who the Holy Spirit is and describe His work in helping, guiding, and empowering believers.

nodes.title: The Second Coming
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the Christian hope that Jesus will return, and describe in broad terms what Scripture teaches about His second coming.

nodes.title: Theological Reasoning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build a reasoned explanation of a doctrine by drawing on multiple Scripture passages and identifying how they support one another.

nodes.title: Modern Theology
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe major movements and questions in modern theology and evaluate them in light of Scripture.

nodes.title: Worldview Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe what a worldview is, contrast a biblical worldview with other worldviews, and explain how core beliefs shape values and choices.

nodes.title: Apologetics (Foundations)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can give basic reasoned answers to common questions about the Christian faith and support them with Scripture and evidence.

nodes.title: Advanced Apologetics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can engage advanced objections to Christianity and construct a well-organized, evidence-based defense of the faith.

nodes.title: Applying Scripture
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can take a biblical principle from a passage and describe a specific way to apply it to everyday life.

nodes.title: Spiritual Disciplines
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name the core spiritual disciplines (prayer, worship, Bible reading) and explain why each helps a believer grow.

nodes.title: Prayer
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what prayer is, describe different kinds of prayer (praise, thanks, asking, confession), and pray in their own words.

nodes.title: Worship
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what worship is and describe ways Christians worship God individually and together.

nodes.title: Devotional Bible Reading
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe a simple habit of daily Bible reading and reflection and explain why it helps a believer grow in faith.

nodes.title: The Fruit of the Spirit
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can list the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5 and give an everyday example of showing one of them.

nodes.title: Stewardship & Service
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that God calls people to use their time, talents, and resources to serve Him and others, and describe a way to serve.

nodes.title: Discipleship
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what it means to follow Jesus as a disciple and describe the practices and commitments of a growing Christian life.

nodes.title: Ethics & Moral Reasoning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply biblical principles to evaluate a moral situation and explain the reasoning behind a right course of action.

nodes.title: Faith in Action
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan and carry out a way to live out their faith through service, witness, or generosity and reflect on its impact.

nodes.title: Church History
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can trace the growth of the Church from the early Church through key events such as the councils, the Reformation, and modern missions.

merges.note: B1 Bible Structure was a coarse Foundations node bundling several distinct assessable ideas. Retained as the base atomic (the Bible is one book of many books, Old and New Testaments, 66 books) and decomposed into B-301 Books of the Bible, B-302 Old & New Testament Divisions (Law/History/Wisdom-Poetry/Prophets; Gospels/Acts/Epistles/Revelation), and B-303 Finding a Verse (Book, Chapter, Verse). B-304 Bible Translations added new alongside them.

B2 Key Bible Stories was a coarse Foundations node. Retained as the base atomic (retell well-known stories, identify the main person and lesson) and split out B-334 Key Bible Events Timeline (arranging major events in chronological order) as an Application-level integrative skill. Character-study nodes B-330 Elijah, B-331 Daniel, B-332 Mary, and B-333 Peter added new in the Key Figures & Events strand to cover the benchmark figures not carried by the OT/NT survey chains (Abraham=B-312, Moses=B-313, David=B-315, Paul=B-326).

B7 Doctrinal Basics was a single coarse node covering all core doctrine. Retained as the base atomic (explain core beliefs about God, Jesus, the Bible, salvation, and the Church) and decomposed into B-341 The Trinity, B-342 Attributes of God, B-343 Sin & Grace, and B-344 The Holy Spirit. Additional doctrine added new: B-340 The Gospel & Salvation (placed early as a Fluency feeder on B4 rather than gated behind full doctrinal basics, so the central gospel message stays accessible) and B-345 The Second Coming.

B14 Spiritual Disciplines bundled several distinct practices. Retained as the umbrella base atomic (name the core disciplines and explain why each helps growth) and decomposed into B-350 Prayer, B-351 Worship, and B-352 Devotional Bible Reading. Following the lifeskills pattern, the base now soft-depends on its components, but the components are NOT hard-locked behind the base: B-350 Prayer and B-351 Worship are Foundations feeders with no hard prereqs, avoiding the stage inversion of gating the earliest devotional practices behind a later umbrella node. B-353 The Fruit of the Spirit and B-354 Stewardship & Service added new in the Christian Living strand.

Structural fix: the original graph was a single linear hard-prereq spine B1->B2->B3->B4->B5->B6->B7->B8->B9->B10->B11->B12->B13->B14->B15->B16 (19 hard edges, 0 soft) plus four leads_to branches (B17->B18, B18->B16, B19->B16, B20->B16), forcing unrelated skills into one chain -- e.g. Memory Verses (B3) before Basic Biblical Themes (B4), Applying Scripture (B9) before all of Theological Reasoning/Worldview/Apologetics, and Advanced Apologetics (B13) hard-locking Spiritual Disciplines (B14) hard-locking Discipleship (B15). That spine was dismantled and re-grouped into nine real strands (Bible Basics & Structure, Bible Study Skills, Old Testament, New Testament, Key Figures & Events, Doctrine & Theology, Christian Living & Discipleship, Apologetics & Worldview, Church History). Directions were corrected on the principle: structure/reading before interpretation before theology, and stories before themes before doctrine. Concretely: B4 Basic Biblical Themes now builds on B2 Key Bible Stories (themes emerge from narrative) rather than on Memory Verses; B7 Doctrinal Basics builds on B4; B8 Biblical Interpretation builds on B5 Understanding Context which builds on B6 Reading Scripture Independently; the reasoning cluster (B10 Theological Reasoning, B11 Worldview Analysis, B12/B13 Apologetics) builds on B7 and B8 rather than on the applied/devotional track. The devotional track (B9 Applying Scripture, B14 Spiritual Disciplines, B15 Discipleship, B16 Faith in Action) was separated from the intellectual track and made to depend on reading/application, not on advanced apologetics. Cross-strand hard locks were converted to soft_deps wherever a genuine content prerequisite did not exist (the graph went from 0 soft deps to a soft-heavy structure); the few remaining cross-strand hard prereqs reflect real content dependencies (e.g. B17 Church History hard-requires B-325 The Early Church/Acts, since church history literally begins there). The four leads_to edges were converted: B17->B18 became B18 hard-on-B10 with soft-on-B17; B18/B19/B20 no longer force into B16. Cross_domain edges to other subjects (E*/L*/LS*/SS* ids) are external to this subject graph and are represented via the cross-domain layer, not as intra-Bible prereqs, so they are not carried into hard_prereqs/soft_deps here. Junk stage-name clusters (Foundations/Fluency/Application/Integration/Mastery) were replaced by the nine topical strands, while stage/stage_id were preserved as the difficulty axis. Benchmarked against a standard K-12 Bible curriculum, 39 new/split skills were added to fill gaps in Bible basics, Old Testament survey, New Testament survey, key figures, doctrine, and Christian living.
